scope: Hunter enemy-red asset preparation only. No team/PvP runtime hookup, no registration/installation, no HUD, no weapon catalog, no geometry redesign.

recolor.method: Visible RGB: m=max(R,G,B), s=(m-min(R,G,B))/m (s=0 at m=0); R=m, G=round(m*(0.11+0.58*(1-s)^2)), B=round(m*(0.22+0.44*(1-s)^2)). Saturated colors become crimson; pale highlights remain warm rose. Alpha unchanged, alpha=0 RGBA unchanged. Same transform for constant tints. No resize or geometry/UV/animation changes.
recolor.embedded_texture_names: stem_enemy.png; slot indices and internal UUIDs preserved, root name/model_identifier suffixed; animation names remain spawn/loop to preserve contracts

excluded.name: hunter/arc_combination_blow
excluded.reason: HunterAbilityVisuals.melee(ARC) returns ItemStack.EMPTY; no ability prop to clone.

excluded.name: bowStage legacy stages
excluded.reason: Current SuperVisuals.bowStage always returns shadow_bow_h28_drawn; releasedBow uses shadow_bow_h28. Only current roots cloned.

excluded.name: BetterModel player limb/steve animations
excluded.reason: Not one of the 8 world VFX roots and not an item dependency; player skin/team tint is separate.

excluded.name: weapon catalog + local HUD
excluded.reason: Explicit user exclusion; only exact reachable ability resources traversed.

integration_notes: Copy payload/src/main/resources as a resource delta only after master review.
BetterModel enemy .bbmodel names must separately be registered/installed if future viewer logic selects them. No code/config wiring is supplied.
Native item definitions and all reachable destiny models/textures are deep clones with _enemy resource IDs.
Current handheld composites already have 2298/2350/1384 mesh nodes; counts are preserved by instruction, not reduced or certified against redesign budgets.
Future PvP needs per-viewer ownership/team selection and duplicate/default suppression; these assets alone do not implement it.

comparison.note: Optional offline static preview only; no native/game claim; not required before integration.
